root_cause: When a focused element inside the trap is removed (e.g., the remove button's li), the focusin handler attempts to restore focus by trying to refocus the previously focused node (state.mostRecentlyFocusedNode) even if it is now detached from the DOM. The tabbableNodes array still contains the removed node, causing findContainerIndex to incorrectly report the node as still contained, so the fallback to the initial focus node is not triggered.
repair_strategy: Modify the fallback in checkFocusIn to only attempt to refocus the MRU node if it is still attached to the document (using isNodeAttached) and still contained in a trap container (using findContainerIndex). Otherwise, fall back to the initial focus node.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus will remain trapped inside the dialog after removing an item, ensuring tab navigation stays within the basket dialog.
functional_risks: Potential side effect of focusing a different element than expected when the MRU node is detached but still focusable (unlikely).
Change may affect behavior when focus escapes due to other reasons; but the fallback to initial focus node is consistent with existing logic for other escape scenarios.
verification_requirements: After applying the change, the specific journey step (pressing Enter on the remove button) should result in focus remaining inside the basket (i.e., #basket:focus-within visible).
Ensure that tabbing still works and focus does not escape when removing other items.
Verify that activating/deactivating the trap still works as expected.
